The test image shows soybean leaves with prominent **interveinal chlorosis** (yellowing between veins while veins stay green) and scattered small reddish-brown spots/lesions. This narrows candidates to: **Sudden_death_syndrome**, **Brown_Stem_Rot**, or **Fusarium**.

Let me view reference images for these top candidates.

The **Brown_Stem_Rot** reference image (train_003) is nearly identical to the test image — both show the same pattern of interveinal chlorosis with scattered small reddish-brown lesions on soybean leaves in a field setting. The SDS reference showed a different presentation (stem with blue fungal growth), and Fusarium showed internal stem vascular tissue.

The test image matches Brown_Stem_Rot's characteristic interveinal chlorosis (yellowing between veins, veins stay green) with small necrotic spots — which is the classic foliar expression of this disease.
